h1: A segmentation week, not a buzz race
room_line: LOBANG BUAYA has the clearest measurable campaign but weak interaction; DJAMIN SETIA SELAMANYA has the sharpest concentration thesis; WARGA RUSUN 609 has the most legible broad hook. None has purchase proof.
coming_kick: Four October 1 titles offer distinct mechanisms: topical historical horror, a Karo cultural event, localized horror-comedy and Bandung humanist comedy-drama.
coming_caveat: Booking remains unresolved across the slate, and public activity cannot establish SAMS demand, session behavior or sustained conversion.
signal_note: Only LOBANG BUAYA has a clean quantified social sample: 5,725 views, 92 likes, zero comments and five shares across ten posts. WARGA RUSUN 609 shows activation without sales; DJAMIN SETIA SELAMANYA and CONJURIG lack attributable samples, which means unavailable—not weak.

eligibility.basis: Present on both M-Tix/Cinema XXI and the SAMS public Coming surface. The SAMS surface is explicitly discovery-only and does not provide the required private owner or Programming confirmation of ordinary eligibility.

coming.meta: Dito Darmawan, Maizura; Global Borneo Entertainment, Bima Sakti Pictures and Imagine: supported by Ferry Maryadi, Mathias Muchus, Bucek Deep and Trie Utami.
coming.logline: Two wounded strangers hiding behind ghost-cosplay personas meet on Bandung’s streets and begin confronting the lives they were trying to escape.
coming.quality: Warm, quirky comedy-drama proposition: captured material promises everyday humor, humanist emotion and musical elements, but every readable assessment is promotional rather than an independent review or screening reaction.
coming.gold: Distinctive local hook, unproven conversion: Bandung street culture and ghost cosplay give the film a clearer identity than generic horror, while comedy, romance-adjacent emotion and music may broaden appeal beyond horror audiences.
coming.promo: Basic launch assets exist, campaign depth is unclear: a 1-minute-46-second trailer was released and the film’s Instagram account is named, but no captured evidence shows roadshows, cast visits, ticket offers or sustained activation.
coming.social: No usable title-bound social signal: both captured keyword samples are dominated by the unrelated The Conjuring franchise, so their views and engagement cannot be attributed to CONJURIG.
coming.demand: Release intent, not purchase intent: sources consistently state an October 1 theatrical release, but the bundle contains no verified showtimes, presale availability, seat movement, ticket sales or clean audience-intent signal.
coming.risk: High false-signal and positioning risk: the name is easily conflated with The Conjuring, while promotional copy may invite a horror reading even though the captured premise is comedy-drama; private SAMS eligibility is also unresolved by this bundle.
coming.bet: If it opens at SAMS, CONJURIG will rank below the same-week domestic median on paid admissions per show through Day 4.
coming.nug: Ghost cosplay is the hook, but the film is a warm Bandung comedy-drama—not supernatural horror.

lanes.read: Two wounded strangers hiding behind ghost-cosplay personas meet on Bandung’s streets and begin confronting the lives they were trying to escape.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: ANTARA describes Piit and Tamy as two people using costumes to hide from personal problems before finding each other.
lanes.decision_consequence: Frame this as a human comedy-drama with a distinctive Bandung cosplay setting, not as conventional supernatural horror.

lanes.read: Recognizable supporting cast, modest lead pull: Dito Darmawan and Maizura lead, supported by Ferry Maryadi, Mathias Muchus, Bucek Deep and Trie Utami; Global Borneo Entertainment, Bima Sakti Pictures and Imagine are named as producers.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Captured full-text reports consistently name the leads, supporting ensemble and three production banners.
lanes.decision_consequence: The ensemble adds familiarity, but the evidence does not establish a lead actor with proven opening-week ticket power.

lanes.read: Warm, quirky comedy-drama proposition: captured material promises everyday humor, humanist emotion and musical elements, but every readable assessment is promotional rather than an independent review or screening reaction.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Director Tubagus Deddy describes a warm Bandung atmosphere, while producer Budi Ismanto emphasizes comedy-drama and musical elements.
lanes.missing_fact: An independent review, verified screening reaction or title-bound audience response assessing the finished film.
lanes.decision_consequence: Use the tone as positioning only; do not upgrade the title for presumed quality.

lanes.read: Distinctive local hook, unproven conversion: Bandung street culture and ghost cosplay give the film a clearer identity than generic horror, while comedy, romance-adjacent emotion and music may broaden appeal beyond horror audiences.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The premise is tied to Bandung’s Comjurig community and combines ghost imagery with comedy-drama, personal healing and music.
lanes.decision_consequence: If eligibility is confirmed, test messaging around Bandung street-culture comedy rather than selling a horror promise the evidence does not support.

lanes.read: Basic launch assets exist, campaign depth is unclear: a 1-minute-46-second trailer was released and the film’s Instagram account is named, but no captured evidence shows roadshows, cast visits, ticket offers or sustained activation.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Multiple captured reports state that the first trailer was released through @conjurig.film.
lanes.decision_consequence: Count the title as publicly launched, but do not treat trailer availability alone as a strong promotional campaign.

lanes.read: No usable title-bound social signal: both captured keyword samples are dominated by the unrelated The Conjuring franchise, so their views and engagement cannot be attributed to CONJURIG.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Seven TikTok and ten Instagram samples were captured, but inspected excerpts concern The Conjuring rather than this Indonesian film.
lanes.missing_fact: Clean title-bound posts, comments and engagement using identity terms such as Dito Darmawan, Maizura or Tubagus Deddy.
lanes.decision_consequence: Discard the captured social metrics from demand judgment; the naming collision makes them actively misleading.

lanes.read: Release intent, not purchase intent: sources consistently state an October 1 theatrical release, but the bundle contains no verified showtimes, presale availability, seat movement, ticket sales or clean audience-intent signal.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The producer and repeated reports confirm the planned October 1 release; purchase-focused searches returned only release announcements.
lanes.missing_fact: Verified ticket availability plus title-bound presale, seat, showtime or purchase-intent evidence.
lanes.decision_consequence: Do not infer opening demand or authorize an exploration floor from the release announcement.

lanes.read: High false-signal and positioning risk: the name is easily conflated with The Conjuring, while promotional copy may invite a horror reading even though the captured premise is comedy-drama; private SAMS eligibility is also unresolved by this bundle.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Every captured social sample was contaminated by The Conjuring, while full-text reports explicitly describe CONJURIG as comedy-drama.
lanes.decision_consequence: Keep the title out of allocation until eligibility is privately confirmed, and require identity-clean demand evidence before any commercial upgrade.

ai_rating.source_confidence: Mixed: identity and release are verified; finished-film quality rests on promotional claims.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Pending: public SAMS Coming presence exists; private booking eligibility is unconfirmed.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: Low: October 1 release is verified; no showtimes, presale, seats or purchase-intent evidence.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Weak: trailer and @conjurig.film exist; sampled social activity belongs to The Conjuring.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: High: name collision and horror mispositioning can create false signals; eligibility remains unresolved.
ai_rating.actionability: Limited: eligibility is unresolved; any later read requires identity-clean paid admissions.

coming.meta: Rafi Sudirman and Erjege Pictures: Claresta Taufan, Chicco Kurniawan, Jourdy Pranata and Marcell Darwin support the ensemble; Rako Prijanto directs.
coming.logline: A young Djamin Ginting rises from colonial-era student to guerrilla leader while balancing family loyalty with Indonesia’s struggle for independence.
coming.quality: Encouraging craft signal, narrow validation: one readable review praises realistic battle audio, period production, makeup and measured pacing, but broader independent corroboration is absent.
coming.gold: Specific cultural-event hook, uncertain scale: the Djamin Ginting story, Karo identity and 1 October release create a timely patriotic proposition, but no evidence proves broad ticket conversion.
coming.promo: Press-led campaign, no proven activation: recent interviews and conference coverage consistently communicate the hero, youth-inspiration and 1 October release story, but no roadshow or ticket offer was captured.
coming.social: No usable film engagement signal: the captured TikTok keyword results contain generic “setia” material and unrelated viral posts, so their large view totals cannot be attributed to this title.
coming.demand: Release intent without purchase proof: a trailer asset and 1 October release announcement exist, but there are no trailer metrics, presales, cinema schedules, seat movement or attributable watch-intent comments.
coming.risk: Primary risk is false confidence from publicity: favorable craft coverage and nationwide-release language may look commercially reassuring, yet SAMS eligibility and purchase-proximate demand remain unverified.
coming.bet: If booked, culturally relevant catchments will outperform the title’s chain-wide median occupancy through Day 4.
coming.nug: The Karo national-hero story and Hari Kesaktian Pancasila timing create a specific cultural-event hook, not proven broad demand.

lanes.read: Historical biopic: a young Djamin Ginting rises from colonial-era student to guerrilla leader while balancing family loyalty with Indonesia’s struggle for independence.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Film Indonesia provides a detailed synopsis covering Djamin’s education, Gyugun service, North Sumatra guerrilla campaign and relationship with Likas Tarigan.
lanes.decision_consequence: The room can position this as a patriotic historical drama with war action and a personal relationship thread, not as a general action spectacle.

lanes.read: Recognizable ensemble, modest star pull: Rafi Sudirman leads with Claresta Taufan, Chicco Kurniawan, Jourdy Pranata and Marcell Darwin; Erjege Pictures produces.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Channel9 directly names Erjege Pictures, director Rako Prijanto and the principal ensemble.
lanes.decision_consequence: Talent supports credible publicity and ensemble appeal, but the evidence does not establish a bankable lead capable of carrying broad opening demand.

lanes.read: Encouraging craft signal, narrow validation: one readable review praises realistic battle audio, period production, makeup and measured pacing, but broader independent corroboration is absent.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Teknogav reports immersive sound, serious period design, convincing makeup and a well-paced narrative after apparently viewing the film.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat quality as a reason to investigate or screen the film, not as justification for a confident commercial floor.

lanes.read: Specific cultural-event hook, uncertain scale: the Djamin Ginting story, Karo identity and 1 October release create a timely patriotic proposition, but no evidence proves broad ticket conversion.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The film is explicitly framed around a Karo national hero and scheduled for 1 October, Hari Kesaktian Pancasila.
lanes.decision_consequence: If SAMS confirms eligibility, test the title as a culturally specific event proposition rather than assuming chain-wide mainstream demand.

lanes.read: Press-led campaign, no proven activation: recent interviews and conference coverage consistently communicate the hero, youth-inspiration and 1 October release story, but no roadshow or ticket offer was captured.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Recent readable coverage includes statements from Rako Prijanto, Riahna Djamin Ginting and Rafi Sudirman tied to the release narrative.
lanes.decision_consequence: Expect basic awareness support, but do not credit the title with an activation-driven uplift unless concrete cinema visits, community partnerships or offers appear.

lanes.read: No usable film engagement signal: the captured TikTok keyword results contain generic “setia” material and unrelated viral posts, so their large view totals cannot be attributed to this title.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Ten TikTok keyword results were captured, but the visible excerpts do not reliably identify DJAMIN SETIA SELAMANYA.
lanes.missing_fact: Film-matched posts, reach, engagement and audience comments from official or clearly attributable uploads.
lanes.decision_consequence: Discard the captured TikTok totals from demand judgment; the room currently has insufficient evidence of genuine social traction.

lanes.read: Release intent without purchase proof: a trailer asset and 1 October release announcement exist, but there are no trailer metrics, presales, cinema schedules, seat movement or attributable watch-intent comments.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The official Cinema XXI-hosted trailer asset is available, while the readable release coverage confirms only the planned date.
lanes.missing_fact: Current presale availability, booked locations and sessions, seat sales, attributable trailer reach and explicit audience watch intent.
lanes.decision_consequence: Do not assign an exploration floor from public demand evidence; first obtain SAMS eligibility and purchase-proximate data.

lanes.read: Primary risk is false confidence from publicity: favorable craft coverage and nationwide-release language may look commercially reassuring, yet SAMS eligibility and purchase-proximate demand remain unverified.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The bundle contains one favorable readable review and repeated release announcements, but no attributable social signal or transaction evidence.
lanes.decision_consequence: Keep the title outside allocation judgment until private SAMS booking truth is confirmed; if confirmed, use a tightly monitored test rather than a publicity-led commitment.

ai_rating.source_confidence: Medium: identity and release facts are solid; positive craft evidence comes from one readable review.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Low: absent from captured SAMS Coming titles, with no current Programming confirmation.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: Low: trailer and release date exist, but presales, schedules, seat movement and watch intent are missing.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Low: press coverage is active, but no activation is proven and captured TikTok posts are not film-attributable.

ai_rating.actionability: Booking-dependent: confirm SAMS eligibility and capture approved sessions and presale movement.

eligibility.basis: Present on both M-Tix/Cinema XXI and the SAMS public Coming surface. The SAMS surface is explicitly discovery-only and does not provide the required private owner or Programming confirmation of ordinary eligibility.

coming.meta: Hanung Bramantyo; Adhya Pictures and Dapur Films: starring Baskara Mahendra, Carissa Perusset, Khiva Iskak, Anya Zen and Mathias Muchus.
coming.logline: In 1964, a newly married military officer investigates ritualistic village murders while a supernatural force terrorizes his wife and points toward a wider conspiracy.
coming.quality: Promising thematic texture, unproven overall quality: a post-screening report supports layered mystery, social criticism and a viewer-recognized anti-corruption theme, but no independent critical verdict was captured.
coming.gold: Timely historical horror with a recognizable filmmaker: the October 1 opening immediately follows the September 30 remembrance window, giving the mystery a sharp topical hook but also narrowing its emotional positioning.
coming.promo: Active campaign, weak conversion proof: captured promotion includes a Lampung screening, a cast media visit and ten recent TikTok campaign posts, but none demonstrates ticket purchase or broad organic advocacy.
coming.social: Visible but shallow social response: ten captured TikTok posts totaled 5,725 views, 92 likes, zero comments and five shares, with one post supplying 3,960 views; the sample is directional and largely campaign-led.
coming.demand: Insufficient evidence of ticket demand: MOPIC carries the title and October 1 date, but the captured page contains no live showtimes, presale status, seat movement, sales volume or sold-out sessions.
coming.risk: Messaging inconsistency is the clearest risk: direct cast statements call the story wholly fictional, while captured campaign posts describe the terror as real, creating avoidable confusion around a politically sensitive setting.
coming.bet: If booked, its timely mystery and Hanung Bramantyo will drive initial trial, but weak engagement will limit Day 4 retention.
coming.nug: A sharp October 1 historical-horror hook is offset by campaign copy calling fictional terror real, creating topicality and confusion together.

lanes.read: In 1964, a newly married military officer investigates ritualistic village murders while a supernatural force terrorizes his wife and points toward a wider conspiracy.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: MOPIC’s captured synopsis directly describes Letnan Soegeng’s investigation, Arum Wangi’s haunting and the ritual behind both threats.
lanes.decision_consequence: The premise is clear, marketable historical horror-mystery rather than a literal reconstruction of the 1965 tragedy.

lanes.read: Hanung Bramantyo is the strongest commercial name; Adhya Pictures and Dapur Films produce, with Baskara Mahendra, Carissa Perusset, Khiva Iskak, Anya Zen and Mathias Muchus in the cast.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: MOPIC directly lists the director, producer, production houses, release date and principal cast.
lanes.decision_consequence: Use Hanung and the ensemble as recognition anchors, while avoiding unsupported claims that the cast alone guarantees demand.

lanes.read: Promising thematic texture, unproven overall quality: a post-screening report supports layered mystery, social criticism and a viewer-recognized anti-corruption theme, but no independent critical verdict was captured.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: IDN Times reported from a screening and quoted one attendee responding to the film’s criticism of abused authority.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat the film as creatively interesting but do not upgrade its commercial posture on quality until independent reviews or broad audience reactions appear.

lanes.read: Timely historical horror with a recognizable filmmaker: the October 1 opening immediately follows the September 30 remembrance window, giving the mystery a sharp topical hook but also narrowing its emotional positioning.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Captured sources consistently establish the 1964 setting, October 1 release, horror-mystery form and Hanung Bramantyo’s authorship.
lanes.decision_consequence: Position it around mystery, horror and abuse-of-power themes; do not sell it as a factual G30S reconstruction or infer mass demand from topicality.

lanes.read: Active campaign, weak conversion proof: captured promotion includes a Lampung screening, a cast media visit and ten recent TikTok campaign posts, but none demonstrates ticket purchase or broad organic advocacy.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: IDN Times captured a screening appearance; Suara.com captured a cast media visit; social capture shows concentrated posting on September 26.
lanes.decision_consequence: Credit the distributor with active promotion, but keep allocation judgment separate because campaign volume has not produced a verified purchase signal.

lanes.read: Visible but shallow social response: ten captured TikTok posts totaled 5,725 views, 92 likes, zero comments and five shares, with one post supplying 3,960 views; the sample is directional and largely campaign-led.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured sample contains exact per-post reach and interaction counts, with no comments across all ten posts.
lanes.decision_consequence: Social activity supports awareness monitoring, not a demand upgrade; the room should wait for organic conversation or transaction evidence.

lanes.read: Insufficient evidence of ticket demand: MOPIC carries the title and October 1 date, but the captured page contains no live showtimes, presale status, seat movement, sales volume or sold-out sessions.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: A cinema title page confirms release proximity, while every purchase-intent metric needed for a demand judgment remains absent.
lanes.missing_fact: Live presale availability, transaction volume, seat occupancy or comparable SAMS booking evidence.
lanes.decision_consequence: Do not convert public presence into an exploration floor; private SAMS eligibility and a real purchase signal must be confirmed before allocation.

lanes.read: Messaging inconsistency is the clearest risk: direct cast statements call the story wholly fictional, while captured campaign posts describe the terror as real, creating avoidable confusion around a politically sensitive setting.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Suara.com quotes Carissa Perusset saying the film is fiction and not inspired by true events; TikTok copy says “cerita nyata” and “Semua terror nya nyata.”
lanes.decision_consequence: Require factual discipline in room language and audience-facing copy; monitor whether confusion becomes backlash rather than treating controversy as free awareness.

ai_rating.source_confidence: High: the premise, identity, release date, campaign activity and sampled social counts are directly supported.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Partial: listed on SAMS public Coming, but private booking and ordinary eligibility remain unconfirmed.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: Low: no presale, showtime, seat movement, transaction volume or comparable SAMS booking evidence was captured.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Weak: active promotion produced 5,725 sampled views, 92 likes, zero comments and five shares across ten posts.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: Elevated: cast statements call the story fictional while campaign captions describe the terror as real.
ai_rating.actionability: Measure only if eligibility and booking are confirmed; current evidence cannot establish initial or sustained demand.

coming.meta: Morgan Oey, Ranty Maria and Rapi Films: ensemble support from Gita Bhebhita, Sarah Sechan, Aming and Dustin Tiffani; directed by Herwin Novianto from Upi's screenplay.
coming.logline: A wealthy student confronts his dead former lover haunting Room 609 while the eccentric residents of her public-housing block resist relocation.
coming.quality: Unproven current-film quality: the localized horror-comedy premise and ensemble offer accessible energy, but the captured full texts are previews or listings, while the social reactions are not independently attributable reviews.
coming.gold: Accessible but execution-dependent proposition: familiar Indonesian horror-comedy, a socially recognizable rusun setting and a broad comedy ensemble create a legible group-viewing hook, while remake familiarity alone does not prove conversion.
coming.promo: Active localized campaign: trailer and poster coverage is reinforced by cast appearances, advance screenings across 14 cities, a Bekasi event and a branded ghost-bus activation; activity is visible, but it remains promotion rather than demand.
coming.social: Uneven early social signal: the ten-post TikTok sample is mostly low-reach campaign material, while one reaction-style ending clip reached 8,980 views and 389 likes; the sample is directional and not representative of broad audience pull.
coming.demand: No proven ticket demand: captured posts invite viewers to secure tickets and promote advance screenings, but the bundle contains no sales, presale velocity, seat occupancy, sold-out shows or attributable purchase-intent evidence.
coming.risk: Primary room risk: SAMS eligibility is unverified, current-film quality remains untested and the visible campaign has not translated into measurable purchase intent; the localized remake and crowded ensemble may work, but execution is the unresolved variable.
coming.bet: If SAMS confirms eligibility, its localized horror-comedy hook should match domestic peers, led by evening and weekend occupancy.
coming.nug: Communal chaos is the edge: a Room 609 haunting collides with a rusun resisting relocation, making the comedy more legible than the remake IP—but conversion is unproven.

lanes.read: A wealthy student must confront his dead former lover haunting Room 609 while the eccentric residents of her public-housing block fight an attempted relocation.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The fetched synopsis consistently joins Bunga's haunting, Arka's broken promise and the residents' resistance to relocation.
lanes.decision_consequence: The film has a clear dual hook—romantic haunting and neighborhood comedy—that can be communicated quickly if SAMS confirms eligibility.

lanes.read: Morgan Oey and Ranty Maria lead Rapi Films' ensemble horror-comedy, supported by Gita Bhebhita, Sarah Sechan, Aming, Dustin Tiffani and other comedy-facing talent; Herwin Novianto directs from Upi's screenplay.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Fetched materials directly identify Rapi Films with Sky Media Films, Vortera Studios and Legacy Pictures, plus the principal cast, director and writer.
lanes.decision_consequence: The recognizable ensemble gives Programming a stronger comedy-led positioning hook than a star-driven prestige proposition.

lanes.read: Unproven current-film quality: the localized horror-comedy premise and ensemble offer accessible energy, but the captured full texts are previews or listings, while the social reactions are not independently attributable reviews.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: One captured TikTok item saying the ending was surprising reached 8,980 views with 389 likes, 16 comments and 12 shares, but its independence and representativeness are unverified.
lanes.missing_fact: A readable independent review or attributable audience assessment from a completed screening of this film.
lanes.decision_consequence: Do not convert the appealing premise or promotional laughter claims into a quality premium; wait for attributable audience evidence or Day 1 behavior.

lanes.read: Accessible but execution-dependent proposition: familiar Indonesian horror-comedy, a socially recognizable rusun setting and a broad comedy ensemble create a legible group-viewing hook, while remake familiarity alone does not prove conversion.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Fetched sources confirm a localized adaptation of Thailand's Buppah Rahtree built around communal reactions, comedy and a relocation conflict.
lanes.decision_consequence: If SAMS confirms the title is bookable, position it around chaotic communal comedy and monitor trial rather than assuming the source IP or genre guarantees demand.

lanes.read: Active localized campaign: trailer and poster coverage is reinforced by cast appearances, advance screenings across 14 cities, a Bekasi event and a branded ghost-bus activation; activity is visible, but it remains promotion rather than demand.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: The captured TikTok sample directly records 14-city advance play, Bekasi cast activity and a Cilegon ghost-bus activation.
lanes.decision_consequence: The campaign supplies usable opening-week awareness, but Programming should require ticket behavior before rewarding its promotional breadth with additional confidence.

lanes.read: Uneven early social signal: the ten-post TikTok sample is mostly low-reach campaign material, while one reaction-style ending clip reached 8,980 views and 389 likes; the sample is directional and not representative of broad audience pull.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Among ten captured posts, the largest reached 8,980 views, while most others remained between 105 and 1,590 views with little commenting or sharing.
lanes.decision_consequence: Treat the standout clip as a creative clue, not a demand breakout; broader independent volume and repeated engagement would be needed to change the room's confidence.

lanes.read: No proven ticket demand: captured posts invite viewers to secure tickets and promote advance screenings, but the bundle contains no sales, presale velocity, seat occupancy, sold-out shows or attributable purchase-intent evidence.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: A captured Bekasi post tells viewers to secure tickets and another promotes 14-city advance play, but neither reports transactions or occupancy.
lanes.missing_fact: Current SAMS eligibility plus site-level presales, paid admissions or comparable fixed-time seat-map evidence.
lanes.decision_consequence: Keep the title at insufficient evidence and do not authorize an exploration floor from public awareness or campaign activity alone.

lanes.read: Primary room risk: SAMS eligibility is unverified, current-film quality remains untested and the visible campaign has not translated into measurable purchase intent; the localized remake and crowded ensemble may work, but execution is the unresolved variable.
lanes.strongest_available_evidence: Fetched coverage establishes a heavily localized remake and ensemble strategy, while captured social evidence shows campaign activity without transactional proof.
lanes.decision_consequence: Resolve private SAMS booking status first; if eligible, use measured opening evidence rather than granting confidence from genre, source IP or promotional scale.

ai_rating.source_confidence: Clear identity and premise: fetched coverage verifies the film, talent, campaign and 1 October release.
ai_rating.sams_relevance: Eligibility unresolved: M-Tix lists it, but captured SAMS Coming titles and owner confirmation do not.
ai_rating.demand_proximity: No proven ticket demand: calls to buy and 14-city advance play contain no sales, occupancy or seat-map evidence.
ai_rating.promo_social_strength: Active campaign, uneven response: concrete activations, but most sampled TikToks stayed below 1,590 views.
ai_rating.risk_pressure: Execution risk remains: remake familiarity, broad talent and campaign scale have not proven quality or conversion.
ai_rating.actionability: Private SAMS eligibility is the gate; if confirmed, Day 1 and Day 4 behavior can test the premise.

attention_heading: Three questions that can move the room

attention.label: Test LOBANG trial versus retention

what_milo_sees.title: LOBANG BUAYA: 309 HARI SEBELUM TRAGEDI BERDARAH
what_milo_sees.insight: Measured: 5,725 sampled views produced only 92 likes, zero comments and five shares. Prediction: October 1 topicality and Hanung Bramantyo can create initial trial, but weak interaction makes Day 4 retention the decisive test. Booking remains unresolved.
